title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-23
content:
Quick notes / brain dump - Alex (GPU ops)

Today focus: triage capacity + networking flakiness on us-west clusters, follow up on hotfix for kv-cache fallback, and get rough numbers for Dedicated Q2 capacity planning.

Top-of-mind TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm host-level NIC firmware (Mellanox) update window with infra-ops (ask Priya) - affects us-west-2c 8xA100 pool. blocked if firmware schedule overlaps canary.
- [ ] Patch and roll PR runtime#891 (kv-cache fallback fix) to canary pool by EOD (small batch, 2 p90 nodes). Samir to run smoke tests.
- [ ] Run capacity stub: estimate Q2 committed capacity needs for Dedicated customers (+15% growth), produce quick table for Friday sync.
- [ ] Investigate intermittent 503s for streaming endpoints (trace id example: 0ff1ce-1234). Looks like connection resets between load-balancer and pod (tcp RST). Capture packet drops and LB error ratios.
- [ ] Add alert: node-level GPU memory fragmentation > 70% for >5m (we saw this spike yesterday on a node running mixed small/big models).

Notes / observations:
- 2026-03-02 evening spike: us-west-2a pool saw p95 latency jump from 110ms -> 310ms for short-chat routes. Correlated with 20% increase in token rate from canary customer. Not sure if autoscaler margin too conservative.
- NVLINK utilization on host gpunode-uw2a-17 at 81% when running long-context workloads (100k windows). Could be impacting other tenants via PCIe congestion.
- NIC errors count (ifInErrors) on sw-uw2a-edge-3: 42 in last 24h; open ticket ENGOPS-732 to network infra.

Commands / quick runbook snippets:
- Check pod logs for kv-cache fallback: kubectl -n runtime logs deployment/runtime-canary -c runtime --since=2h | grep kv-cache
- Capture netstats on affected node: sudo ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "err|drop"
- Quick GPU mem fragmentation check (on node): nvidia-smi dmon -s u | head -n 20  # look for mem utilization vs. free pages

Capacity planning quick calc (rough):
- Current committed Dedicated GPUs: 1,280 (across regions)
- Current avg utilization (prod peak): 62% token-equivalent
- Q2 forecast assumptions: +15% customer growth; caching improvements reduce unit tokens by 6%
- Ballpark need = 1280 * 1.15 * 0.94 ≈ 1,385 -> round to 1,400 GPUs for commit ask (present as ranges 1,350-1,450).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is the autoscaler policy for canary pools inheriting the same cooldowns as prod? (if yes, reduce cooldown from 5m -> 90s for short-burst traffic)
- Can we schedule firmware window for uc-west without impacting the canary rollout? (Priya to confirm)
- Confirm whether kv-cache fallback in PR#891 introduces extra latency for small requests. Samir to add microbench.

Meeting notes/next steps:
- 10:30 sync with infra-networking: show pcap & NIC errors, ask for hotfix plan.
- 14:00 runtime canary deploy window - coordinate Samir for smoke tests and rollback plan.
- Friday capacity sync: prepare 1-slide deck with numbers above + sensitivity to caching improvements (email to product-dedicated).

Misc scratch items (notes to self):
- Save example traces to /tmp/trace-uw2a-20260303.tar.gz then upload to ENGOPS ticket.
- Remind CS to postpone Dedicated marketing email if we expect capacity constraints in Q2 (cc: Elaine).
- TODO: write a short postmortem template for streaming 503 incidents (include net, kv-cache, autoscaling, model fallback sections).

Random quick links:
- Stack: runtime canary logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/runtime/canary
- ENGOPS ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/ENGOPS-732
- Slack: #gpu-ops

End of scratchpad.

-- Alex
